text: Where could your IT skills take you?
Imagine building a career in Japan, learning a new language, and working with people from different backgrounds.
For Cambodian students, this is more than a dream.
It is the opportunity offered by the Japanese IT Pathway Program.
The Japanese IT Pathway Program prepares Cambodian IT students for professional careers in Japan.
Over two years, students first focus on learning Japanese, then develop their IT skills through classes conducted in Japanese.
Along the way, they practice communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and the professional habits expected in Japanese workplaces.
Our goal is not simply to help students pass a language test.
It is to help them become IT professionals who can communicate, contribute to a team, and continue growing in Japan.
This opportunity exists because the Cambodian government believes in the potential of its young people.
With financial support from the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, M P T C, this program makes specialized Japanese language and IT education accessible to students.
This is more than support for individual careers.
It reflects the government's hope that Cambodian students will gain international experience, strengthen their abilities, and contribute to Cambodia's future.
The government is investing in education because it believes your growth matters.
Your education is an investment in the future of Cambodia.
This government support gives you a valuable opportunity.
Your university, your teachers, Next Make, and the government are working together to create an environment where you can learn and grow.
But there is one thing they cannot do for you.
They cannot make the effort for you.
Learning Japanese takes patience. Developing IT skills takes practice.
Some days will be difficult.
What matters is attending class, asking questions, and continuing to learn, even when things are challenging.
The opportunity is being provided.
What you do with it is up to you.
Now, let's hear from two CADT students who have completed their first year of Japanese language study.
You have just heard from two students after their first year of Japanese language study.
They are still on their journey.
But their experiences show what dedication and consistent effort can achieve.
The Cambodian government has helped create this opportunity.
Your university, teachers, and Next Make are here to support you.
We hope you will appreciate this support and show your gratitude through your actions.
Attend class. Keep learning. Support each other.
Your future will not be built in a single day.
It will be built through the effort you make, day after day.
The opportunity is here.
Your future begins with your commitment.
Welcome to the Japanese IT Pathway Program.
